messages:
tara: heads up — bringing up arachne17b (17B) int4 canary on batch pool B. Seeing intermittent OOMs during multi-turns with default max_new_tokens=1024.

sam: logs?

tara: pasted snippet from the worker logs: 
```bash
2026-03-22T16:12:33Z worker-42 OOM on allocate 1.2G for KV cache
stack: alloc_chunk -> slab_alloc -> gpu_mem_reserve
context: prompt_len=4200, batch=4, max_new_tokens=1024, prefetch=true
```

jules: looks like KV cache growth + batching + prefetch = slab fragmentation. Perf counters show gpu_mem_frag rising ~0.34 -> 0.67 at the spike.

kai: agree. quick mitigation: batch_size=1, prefetch=false, max_new_tokens=256, and lower kv_evict_threshold to 0.6 to force earlier trim.

tara: launching a canary with those settings now. payload used for the canary: 
```json
{"model":"arachne17b-int4","pool":"B","batch_size":1,"prefetch":false,"max_new_tokens":256,"kv_evict_threshold":0.6}
```

ops-bot: deploy started: job_id=deploy-4571 state=rolling (canary 10 instances)

sam: also add a synthetic longprompt test (context ~8k tokens) to try to reproduce deterministically.

tara: quick update — after 12 canary runs no OOMs. tail latency increased ~30ms median but stable, and gpu_mem_frag settled ~0.35.

jules: good. we still need to quantify quality impact of int4 + lower max_new_tokens. Please enqueue evals (A/B) against fp16 baseline.

tara: evals queued as e-9832 (700 samples, multi-turn). Early metrics: ~0.8% increase in perplexity across the set, small shift in BLEU/QA F1 for a narrow subset.

kai: acceptable for majority of traffic, but add a soft-throttle policy: if mem_frag > 0.55 then auto-reduce max_new_tokens to 128 and route to smaller model variant as fallback. Also add alarm for >3 OOMs within 5m.

tara: created runbook entry and RFC link: https://redwood.example/runbooks/arachne17b-canary-oom (notes + rollback steps).

sam: SGTM. rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 50% with 30m observation windows. Watch mem_frag, tail-latency (p95/p99), and eval regression deltas.

jules: one more note — when we try re-enabling prefetch for perf, enable slab_align pad=256k (slab padding) to reduce small-allocation churn. That reduced fragmentation on a previous bring-up.

tara: will add slab_align pad and a prefetch A/B later. For now merging canary patch (settings above) and will follow up with evals and metrics in 24h. Thanks @kai @sam @jules :thumbsup:

kai: +1 — if anything pops up I'll pause rollout and revert to fp16 pool.

ops-bot: deploy finished: job_id=deploy-4571 state=completed (canary healthy)

tara: final note — actionable items: 1) add soft-throttle alarm + automated reduction to 128, 2) update onboarding checklist to run longprompt synthetic tests, 3) schedule prefetch+slab_align experiment. I'll create tickets.

sam: thanks, will track tickets and add to next oncall handoff.

jules: echo — nice triage.
